# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# report_date
# The .Rmd relied on report_date already existing in the global environment
# (00_Run the report.R defined it before rmarkdown::render). Quarto renders in
# a fresh R session that cannot see that global, so the date is passed in as a
# parameter: 00_Run the report.R calls
#   quarto::quarto_render(..., execute_params = list(report_date = ...))
# which arrives here as params$report_date. This only affects HOW the date is
# supplied, not the report content.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
if (is.null(params$report_date))
  stop("report_date not supplied — set it via execute_params in 00_Run the report.R")
report_date <- as.Date(params$report_date)

```{r highlight}
# officedown's rdocx implicitly merged a printed ftext (key_points) with a
# following fp_par (header_par) into ONE shaded paragraph, so "Key Points"
# rendered inside the yellow bar. Quarto's docx writer does not merge them,
# which left "Key Points" above an empty yellow bar. Combining them explicitly
# with fpar() reproduces the .Rmd result. (Uses the same objects sourced from
# 0_header.R / 0_style.R — no change to those scripts.)
fpar(key_points, fp_p = header_par)
```
